item_read_reviews.current_claim_excerpt:
## Definition

Let $\mathcal C$ be a fusion category over $\mathbb C$ in the sense of
[[def-fusion-and-multifusion-category]]. A **dagger structure** assigns to every
morphism $f:X\to Y$ a morphism $f^\dagger:Y\to X$, conjugate-linearly, with
$(g\circ f)^\dagger=f^\dagger\circ g^\dagger$ and
$(f^\dagger)^\dagger=f$. A **unitary fusion category** is such a fusion
category equipped with this dagger so that every morphism space is a
finite-dimensional normed space, composition is submultiplicative,
$\|f^\dagger\|=\|f\|$, and $\|f^\dagger f\|=\|f\|^2$. Thus each
$\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(X)$ is a finite-dimensional $C^*$-algebra.
Positive endomorphisms are the elements of its usual $C^*$-positive cone
(equivalently $u^\dagger u$ for an endomorphism $u$); in particular, if $c$ is
simple and $\operatorname{End}(c)=\mathbb C\operatorname{id}_c$, then
$\lambda\operatorname{id}_c$ is positive exactly when $\lambda\ge0$. For any
morphism $f:X\to Y$, $f^\dagger f$ is positive in $\operatorname{End}(X)$;
also require $f^\dagger f=0$ to imply $f=0$. Semisimple direct-sum
decompositions can be chosen orthogonally:
their inclusions $i_j$ satisfy $i_j^\dagger i_k=0$ for $j\ne k$,
$i_j^\dagger i_j=\operatorname{id}$, and $\sum_j i_j i_j^\dagger=\operatorname{id}$.
Tensor product preserves daggers:
$(f\otimes g)^\dagger=f^\dagger\otimes g^\dagger$. Its associator and unit
constraints are **unitary**, meaning $\alpha^\dagger=\alpha^{-1}$,
$\lambda^\dagger=\lambda^{-1}$, and $\rho^\dagger=\rho^{-1}$.

The underlying fusion category is rigid, so its evaluation and coevaluation
morphisms satisfy the duality zig-zag identities. Those morphisms are not
required to be unitary isomorphisms. A braiding is additional structure; when
it is specified as a **unitary braiding**, each component satisfies
$c_{X,Y}^\dagger=c_{X,Y}^{-1}$. Positivity and unitarity are extra structure,
not consequences of the fusion rules or of the braid relations alone.

candidate_boundary_cases_reviewed.actual_evidence: The Definition admits zero morphisms and empty orthogonal sums in a fusion category, but excludes degenerate dagger positivity by f†f=0⇒f=0; evaluation/coevaluation need not be unitary isomorphisms.
Associator and unit constraints are structural maps, not an interval-valued family or a path with free endpoints.
Orthogonal semisimple decompositions are part of the finite-category structure; this Definition does not choose from an arbitrary indexed family of nonempty sets.

## Definition

Let $a,b,c$ be simple objects of a unitary fusion category
$\mathcal C$ ([[def-qc-tqc-unitary-fusion-category]]). The **fusion
multiplicity** is

$$N_{ab}^c:=\dim_{\mathbb C}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(a\otimes b,c),$$

and the corresponding **fusion multiplicity space** is

$$V_{ab}^c:=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(a\otimes b,c).$$

Since $c$ is absolutely simple
([[def-absolutely-simple-object]]), each $f,g\in V_{ab}^c$ has a unique scalar
$\langle f,g\rangle$ satisfying
$f\circ g^\dagger=\langle f,g\rangle\operatorname{id}_c$. This fixes the
inner-product convention to be linear in the first variable. The next local
theorem proves that this pairing is positive definite. No multiplicity-free
assumption is made: $N_{ab}^c$ may be any nonnegative integer.

## Definition

Let $\mathcal C$ be a unitary ribbon fusion category. An object $x$ is
**transparent** if for every simple object $y$ the double braiding

$$c_{y,x}\circ c_{x,y}:x\otimes y\longrightarrow x\otimes y$$

is the identity. By naturality and additivity, the double braiding on a finite
direct sum is block diagonal with the double braidings on its simple summands;
therefore an object is transparent exactly when each simple summand is
transparent. Finite direct sums include the empty sum, so the zero object is
transparent. The category is **modular**, or **nondegenerate**, when its
transparent simple objects consist only of the tensor unit, equivalently when
its transparent objects are exactly the finite direct sums of the tensor unit.
This condition is additional to the existence of fusion spaces and a unitary
braid action.

The double braiding is tested against every simple y for a fixed object x; no geometric endpoints or limiting process occur.

sums are orthogonal. Define tensor product on simple labels by the fusion rules

the adjoint projection $(i_{ab}^c)^\dagger:a\otimes b\to c$; retain
$i_{ab}^c$ itself for the coevaluation construction below. On simple-label
blocks, tensor a pair
of morphism matrices by their Kronecker product on multiplicity coordinates
and by the identity on each simple fusion channel; extend over direct sums.

every F or R coordinate involving $\mathbf1$ is the identity. Put

$$\phi=\frac{1+\sqrt5}{2},\qquad u=\phi^{-1},\qquad v=\phi^{-1/2}.$$

## Definition

Let $m\ge2$ and let $\mathcal H=(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes m}$. A **Majorana
system of length $2m$** is a family of operators
$\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_{2m}\in\operatorname{End}(\mathcal H)$ satisfying
$$\gamma_j^*=\gamma_j,\qquad \gamma_j^2=I,\qquad \gamma_j\gamma_k=-\gamma_k\gamma_j\quad(j\ne k).$$
Its parity operator is $\Pi=i^m\gamma_1\cdots\gamma_{2m}$. For each adjacent
pair, put
$$Q_1(j)=\frac{I-i\gamma_j\gamma_{j+1}}2,\qquad Q_\psi(j)=\frac{I+i\gamma_j\gamma_{j+1}}2,\qquad U_j=\exp\!\left(-\frac\pi4\gamma_j\gamma_{j+1}\right).$$

A **Majorana–Ising exchange interface** on a fixed parity sector consists of
such a system, a choice $\eta\in\{1,-1\}$ and the sector
$\mathcal H_\eta=\ker(\Pi-\eta I)$, together with the following explicit
model-identification hypotheses for every $1\le j<2m$: the Ising pair-charge
projections are identified with $Q_1(j),Q_\psi(j)$, and the exchange is
$R_1Q_1(j)+R_\psi Q_\psi(j)$ with the same relative phase
$R_\psi/R_1=i$. The last identity is required for all adjacent pairs as part
of the interface; the three-anyon supplier below establishes it only in its
stated sector and does not prove this all-$m$ identification.

## Definition

Fix $L\ge3$, $J_e,J_m>0$, a unit vector $\psi$ in the toric code space, and
a specified nontrivial logical Pauli representative $Q$. An **elementary
Pauli path to $Q$** is a finite sequence $E_0,\ldots,E_T$ with $E_0=I$,
$E_T$ a scalar-phase multiple of $Q$, and
$E_{r+1}=P_rE_r$, where each $P_r$ is $X$, $Y$, or $Z$ on a single edge and
the identity on every other edge.

For any prefix Pauli $E$, define its energy excess
$\varepsilon(E):=\langle E\psi,H_LE\psi\rangle-E_{\rm code}$, where
$E_{\rm code}:=-L^2(J_e+J_m)$ is the energy of every code vector. The
**Pauli-path energy barrier** of $Q$ is

$$\mathcal B_L(Q):=\min_{(E_0,\ldots,E_T)}\max_{0\le r\le T}\varepsilon(E_r),$$

where the minimum ranges over elementary Pauli paths to $Q$. This is a
finite-code energy quantity; it is not a thermal lifetime.

representative set $\operatorname{Irr}(\mathcal C)$ of
[[def-qc-tqc-fusion-tree-basis]]. Fix ordered inputs
$a_1,\ldots,a_n\in\operatorname{Irr}(\mathcal C)$, $n\ge1$, a
parenthesized fusion tree, and a total charge
$c\in\operatorname{Irr}(\mathcal C)$ for which the fusion space is nonzero. Simple charges, multiplicity bases, and
admissible fusion-tree vectors have the conventions of
[[def-qc-tqc-fusion-tree-basis]]. An encoded input subspace is specified by a
fixed-charge isometry as in [[def-qc-tqc-fixed-charge-encoding]]. Each task
instance supplies either an initial unit vector in that subspace as an abstract
quantum input, or a finite state-preparation procedure whose specified output
is that vector and whose preparation operations and ancillas are recorded.
The instance also gives a nonnegative rational error threshold and specifies
the correctness relation and metric to which it applies.

A **finite anyon decision task** is a promise pair $(Y,N)$ of disjoint sets of
binary strings with domain $D=Y\cup N$, together with a finite encoding of
admissible fusion-tree input labels; a solver must answer yes on $Y$ and no on
$N$, with no obligation outside $D$. A **finite anyon search task** is a domain
$D$ and a finite-string witness relation, with a valid witness required only
for encoded inputs in $D$. The input record states the number and order of
strands, the finite alphabet of positive and inverse Artin generators
available to the solver, any prescribed finite braid word, and the finite set
of adjacent fusion-measurement locations.
For distinct input charges, an adjacent exchange has the typed unitary
F/R action from the current ordered-list fusion space to the space for the
list with those charges exchanged; track that list after every generator.
These colored maps and their Artin relations are supplied by
[[thm-qc-tqc-gauge-covariance]]. If a single-space $B_n$ representation is
required for the physical-interface record
[[def-qc-tqc-physical-braid-interface]], use the finite orthogonal direct
sum of fusion spaces over all distinct orderings of the fixed input
multiset, with the same total $c$. Each generator maps each summand to its
exchanged-list summand by the typed unitary; its inverse reverses that
map. The colored Artin relations on each summand give the relations on
the direct sum, hence a unitary $B_n$ action. Record the occupied summand
and interpret measurements in its declared fusion-tree basis. Identical
charges give the usual single fixed-space action. The physical-interface
record specifies the mathematical action and separately states its
physical realization hypotheses. The
state-preparation field is an abstract task input and does not assert that a
physical device prepares the state or realizes the braid. Input length and
correctness-on-promises follow [[def-qa-task-and-promise-domain]].

$$\bigl(L_{\rm in},\ N_{\rm any},\ |b|,\ N_{\rm prep},\ N_{\rm anc},\ N_{\rm meas},\ B_{\rm out},\ b_{\max},\ t_{\rm cl},\ T_H,\ \epsilon_{\rm op},\epsilon_{\rm tr},\epsilon_{\rm meas},\ell_{\rm leak},\ p_{\rm leak},\ N_{\rm phase},\ t_{\rm phase}\bigr).$$
Here $L_{\rm in}$ is the complete finite classical input-description bit
length, including the declared task, state/preparation descriptions when
classically encoded, and tolerance descriptions; a directly supplied quantum
input is not assumed to have a finite classical coordinate description;
$N_{\rm any}$ is the number of ordered simple-charge strand labels in the
fusion-space instance; and $|b|$ is the number of braid-generator occurrences
(inverse generators count as one). $N_{\rm prep}$ counts elementary
operations in the declared preparation procedure, while $N_{\rm anc}$ counts
the ancillary anyons or other physical ancilla systems used by preparation or
computation. If the initial state is supplied directly as an abstract quantum
input with no preparation interface, $N_{\rm prep}$ is “not applicable”, not
silently set to zero; $N_{\rm anc}$ still records any declared solver ancillas
(zero if none, or “not applicable” if no physical ancilla model is supplied).
$N_{\rm meas}$ is the number of fusion measurements,
and $B_{\rm out}$ is the total bit length of their classical outcome record
under its declared finite encoding (zero when no measurement occurs). The
largest unary precision query to a certified matrix name is $b_{\max}$; $t_{\rm cl}$
is the classical bit time used by search and postprocessing. $T_H$ is the total
Hamiltonian evolution time over the run in the declared physical time unit;
it is “not applicable” for an abstract braid-only model without Hamiltonian
evolution. The error coordinates $\epsilon_{\rm op},\epsilon_{\rm tr},
\epsilon_{\rm meas},\ell_{\rm leak},p_{\rm leak}$ are respectively a stated
operator-norm approximation bound, an independent in-band transport bound,
an implementation-to-ideal-measurement total-variation bound, and leakage

corrections and their classical control cost. Circuit description and

On one target qubit, $I_2$ and $-I_2$ differ only by a global phase and
induce the same standalone ray and outcome probabilities. Controlled access
changes the comparison. With control first,
$$C(I_2)=I_4,\qquad C(-I_2)=\begin{pmatrix}I_2&0\\0&-I_2\end{pmatrix} =Z\otimes I_2.$$
On input $|+\rangle|0\rangle$, these give $|+\rangle|0\rangle$ and
$|-\rangle|0\rangle$. Measuring the control in the $X$ basis is
respectively deterministic for $+$ and $-$, so the total-variation distance
is one. Thus projective equivalence of an isolated braid gate is not
interchangeable with equality under coherent control.

The two gates are genuine unitary scalars±I2 and the input is normalized; no zero state or singular controlled operator is used.
There is one controlled operation and a final X measurement, with no continuously indexed physical path.
The matrices, |+0> input and measurement basis are fixed, so the counterexample is explicit.
The witness refutes substitution of projective equality under coherent control; it asserts no equivalence between all controlled computations and standalone phase classes.

## Definition

Let $\mathcal C$ be a fusion category over $\mathbb C$, so it is finite semisimple, rigid, monoidal, and has simple unit [[def-fusion-and-multifusion-category]]. Let $a,b,c$ be simple objects and let $n\ge0$. Fix one representative of each simple isomorphism class for the internal path labels; the external objects $a,b,c$ need not equal their representatives. Set $T_0=b$ and recursively fix the left-associated parenthesization $T_{j+1}:=T_j\otimes a$. The **fixed-boundary anyonic path space** is

$$H_{a,n;b,c}:=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(c,T_n).$$

For simple labels $x,y$, define the split multiplicity space $W_{x,a}^y:=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(y,x\otimes a)$. For $n\ge1$, a fusion path is a sequence of simple labels $x_0=b,x_1,\ldots,x_n=c$, with $x_1,\ldots,x_{n-1}$ drawn from the fixed representative set, together with, for every $1\le j\le n$, one basis index $\mu_j$ in a chosen basis $B_{x_{j-1},a}^{x_j}$ of $W_{x_{j-1},a}^{x_j}$. The basis index is retained even when distinct indices have the same adjacent labels. Fusion rules are the nonnegative integers $N_{x a}^{y}$ in $[x][a]=\sum_yN_{x a}^{y}[y]$ [[def-fusion-rules]].

For $n=0$, there is no path if $b\not\cong c$. If $b\cong c$, fix an isomorphism $u_{c,b}:c\to b$ and take it as the single empty-path vector (use $u_{b,b}=\operatorname{id}_b$ when the objects coincide). In the unitary setting choose this isomorphism unitary.

For $n\ge1$, if $i_j\in B_{x_{j-1},a}^{x_j}$ is the selected inclusion $x_j\to x_{j-1}\otimes a$, define the path composite by $\gamma_0:=\operatorname{id}_b$ and $\gamma_j:=(\gamma_{j-1}\otimes\operatorname{id}_a)\circ i_j:x_j\to T_j$. For $x_n=c$, $\gamma_n$ is a vector in $H_{a,n;b,c}$. The next lemma proves these composites form a basis and computes the dimension. No Hilbert-space or physical Hamiltonian structure is part of this definition.

candidate_boundary_cases_reviewed.actual_evidence: At n=0 nonisomorphic b,c give the zero Hom space with no paths; isomorphic unequal b,c use a chosen typed isomorphism, not id_b.

The Definition supplies finite vertex bases and a chosen c→b isomorphism only when b≅c. A unitary choice is required in the unitary setting; its existence is justified by the separately proved Hilbert-path theorem, not by a nonexistent local numbered step.
In the Definition at n=0, an empty-path vector exists only in Hom(c,b) for isomorphic simple b,c; nonisomorphic b,c explicitly have no path.
In the Definition at n=0, b≅c supplies a chosen isomorphism u_{c,b}:c→b as the single path vector, including unequal isomorphic external objects.

## Definition

Let $\mathcal C$ be a fusion category with unit $\mathbf1$. Its Grothendieck fusion ring $K_0(\mathcal C)$ is the free abelian group on simple isomorphism classes, with multiplication induced by tensor product and coefficients given by the fusion rules of [[def-fusion-rules]].

- An object $X$ is **tensor-invertible** if there is an object $Y$ with $X\otimes Y\cong\mathbf1$ and $Y\otimes X\cong\mathbf1$.
- A class $[X]$ is a **fusion-ring unit** if it has a two-sided multiplicative inverse in $K_0(\mathcal C)$; that inverse may have negative integer coefficients in the simple-object basis.
- A linear operator is **invertible** only relative to a specified vector space $H$ and operator $T:H\to H$: it must have a two-sided inverse $S:H\to H$ with $ST=TS=I_H$.

These definitions concern different objects: categorical tensor product, a ring with virtual classes, and a chosen representation on a vector space.

candidate_boundary_cases_reviewed.actual_evidence: The operator definition is relative to a specified vector space, including the zero space with its unique two-sided identity map; virtual negative coefficients in a ring inverse need not define an inverse object.
Three distinct inverse definitions are given, but no equivalence between categorical tensor invertibility, virtual fusion-ring units and operator invertibility is asserted.

Let $a$ be a self-dual simple object with $N_{aa}^{\mathbf1}=1$. Choose a unit vector $v:\mathbf1\to a\otimes a$ spanning the one-dimensional vacuum split space and let $d_a>0$ be its positive spherical dimension.

A **normalized vacuum-channel self-duality datum** is a supplied pair of maps $\operatorname{coev}:\mathbf1\to a\otimes a$ and $\operatorname{ev}:a\otimes a\to\mathbf1$ of the form

$$\operatorname{coev}=\sqrt{d_a}\,v,\qquad \operatorname{ev}=\kappa_a\sqrt{d_a}\,v^\dagger,$$

where $\kappa_a\in\{+1,-1\}$ and the two duality zig-zag identities hold after the self-duality identification, using the left-dual convention of [[def-left-dual-and-right-dual-object]]. We call $\kappa_a$ the **Frobenius–Schur sign in this normalized cup/cap convention**. It is not a braiding or $R$-symbol phase.

## Definition

Fix a fusion-path space with repeated simple site charge $a$, a position $i$ with two adjacent $a$-labels, and a simple output $s$ of $a\otimes a$, chosen from the fixed internal representative set of [[def-anyonic-fusion-path-space]]. Choose bases in the split spaces $\operatorname{Hom}(z,x\otimes y)$ at every vertex of the trees used below, retaining the fixed path vertex bases on the fixed tree. In the tree basis where this adjacent pair is fused first, let $\Pi_s$ be the projection onto the direct summand with pair output $s$, acting as the identity on every multiplicity index inside that channel and as zero on all other pair outputs. Let $A_i:T_{\mathrm{fixed}}\to T_{\mathrm{pair}}$ be a typed composite of associators and their inverses carrying the fixed path tree to this pair-first tree, without permuting the ordered inputs (including the boundary charge). In the split-tree bases of $\operatorname{Hom}(c,T)$, let $F_i$ be the matrix of $h\mapsto A_i\circ h$, with target coordinates as rows and source coordinates as columns. The proof below constructs these bases and proves invertibility in any complex fusion category. Define the **local channel projector** in the fixed path basis by

$$P_{i,s}:=F_i^{-1}\Pi_sF_i.$$

This is an idempotent for any fusion category because $F_i$ is invertible. In a unitary fusion category with orthonormal tree bases, $F_i$ is unitary and $P_{i,s}$ is an orthogonal projection. The channel projection includes every multiplicity coordinate; the definition has no multiplicity-free restriction. The split Hom convention here is $\operatorname{Hom}(c,T)$, as in [[def-anyonic-fusion-path-space]]. In the unitary case with adjoint vertex bases, each local left-to-right split recoupling matrix is the entrywise conjugate of the QC25 inverse-precomposition F matrix, as proved below; they agree for the displayed real Fibonacci and Ising blocks.

$$\mathcal H_L:=\bigoplus_{b\in\operatorname{Irr}(\mathcal C)}H_{D,L;b,b},$$

using the fixed-boundary path spaces of [[def-anyonic-fusion-path-space]] and the orthogonal Hilbert direct-sum inner product. The union of their fusion-path bases, supplied as orthonormal bases by [[thm-anyonic-path-space-is-hilbert-under-unitarity]], is the cyclic path basis: a path in the $b$ summand has $x_1=b$, $x_{L+1}=x_1$, and retains every elementary fusion index. $$P_{2j-1}|_H=(1+X_j)/2,\quad P_{2j}|_H=(1+Z_jZ_{j+1})/2,$$
$$P_{2j-1}|_{\bar H}=(1+Z_jZ_{j+1})/2,\quad P_{2j}|_{\bar H}=(1+X_{j+1})/2.$$
